tables.text_helper: Table 401, "TAMP interconnection", in section 40.3.2 (TAMP pins and internal signals) on page 1600. Columns: Signal name, Source/Destination. 9 data row(s). Notes: 1. This monitoring must be enabled by setting LSECSSON in RTC domain control register (RCC_RTCCR).; 2. This monitoring must be enabled by setting HSECSSON in RCC control register (RCC_CR).; 3. Only TR.

rows: rtc_tamp_evt used to generate a timestamp event

The tamp_potential signal is used to block the read and write accesses to 
the device secrets listed hereafter:
• Backup registers
• SRAM2
The RHUK (root hardware unique key) in system flash memory hardware 
bus to SAES is blocked.
The tamp_potential signal is used to erase the device secrets listed 
hereafter:
• ICACHE content
• SAES, AES, HASH, CCB peripherals
• PKA including PKA SRAM
The device secrets access is blocked when erase is ongoing.

The tamp_confirmed signal is used to erase the device secrets listed 
hereafter:
• Backup registers
• SRAM2
• ICACHE content
• SAES, AES, HASH, CCB peripherals
• PKA including PKA SRAM
The device secrets access is blocked when erase is ongoing.
The RHUK (root hardware unique key) in system flash memory hardware 
bus to SAES is blocked.
Cryptographic peripherals fault (AES or SAES or PKA or TRNG)(3)
IWDG reset when tamper flag is set (potential tamper timeout)
notes: 1. This monitoring must be enabled by setting LSECSSON in RTC domain control register (RCC_RTCCR).
2. This monitoring must be enabled by setting HSECSSON in RCC control register (RCC_CR).
